scope: Every current selection has an inventory row and all numerical curves receive structural checks. Source documentation was reviewed at family/configuration level using retained same-session evidence plus one bounded fresh historical mainline review. This is not independent re-transcription of every inherited table cell or hardware validation.

method.connectedDataCapability: Only a blocking intake form is exposed; no computational/query tool. Local reproducible Python/Node used for catalog tables; no separate Data app created.
method.sourceHierarchy: Supplied catalog controls selection list; exact manufacturer-authored revision controls technical facts; archived manufacturer copies remain labeled; generic product page is not a replacement for original numerical source.

automatedChecks: Finite nonnegative ordered rows and declared-domain coverage
Terminal taps have no through path
Nominal does not exceed maximum at shared printed points
Cable inner + outer equals loop resistance where all three published
Active/node/power registry coverage and no orphan mappings
All gathered technical source URLs have HTTP(S) syntax
Fresh SA mainline exact-model printed-row comparison
countsQualification: The full catalog counts include retired compatibility records; currentSelectionCounts excludes them. These are selection records, not distinct physical units/models; RF and power selections can describe the same equipment. Curve count includes input-current curves but excludes the eight companion watt tables, matching qa/catalog-audit.cjs convention.

findings.issue: Actual installed equipment identity remains user-confirmed; family title alone is insufficient for split, selected output, supply, firmware, control and source revision.
UBT main/aux RF and three UBT power presets are retired from current pickers/workflows; retained only for legacy saved-job readback. HGBT and passive unbalanced three-way outputs remain current.
Exact Quantum18 LE and BA setup manuals remain unavailable; EN9000 commissioning guide requires manufacturer customer access; exact legacy GaN 42/54 source remains unresolved.
Some legacy cable PDFs are unavailable or product-family fallbacks. Original curve/DC source is preserved separately; fallback page availability does not certify numeric cells.

Passive point interpolation is linear and cable interpolation is square-root frequency between printed points; these are estimates, not measured responses. Source band gaps stay unavailable unless the individual curve explicitly declares adjacent-maximum budgeting.

Printed band upper endpoints now return their source bound; exactly 21 legacy SA Multimedia maximum-through curves carry adjacent-maximum fractional-gap policy. Current source inspected; new runtime check recorded separately.

Scientific-Atlanta Multimedia mainline original archived document revision recovered and all 72 printed maximum insertion-loss cells plus 3 nominal coupling values matched; no numeric source edits needed.
15 custom-data RF selections need exact entered loss; 6 manual power selections need entered load. Missing manufacturer table is not zero. Cable-only is an explicit zero equipment path.
Current curves cannot establish true watts or PF when companion real-power values are absent; passing-current and supply maximum ratings are not station consumption.

App RF calculations are limited to 5–1800MHz even when a preserved source table extends to 1825/2000/2050MHz. Table ranges do not automatically establish safe operating voltage or local acceptance targets.

Built-in cable attenuation and loop resistance use documented engineering temperature factors; passive and equipment load temperature effects are not automatically modeled. Custom actual-condition tables are not corrected twice.

manualRegistry.title: GainMaker HGD · OEM AGC setup · historical Cisco manual
manualRegistry.sections: Chapter 3: pp46–50 preparation; pp51–58 manual setup; pp58–64 thermal setup; AGC pad p56/p62
manualRegistry.scope: Exact 1 GHz GainMaker HGD module family; verify installed split and conventional OEM control option. Not ACI DSIM. HGD 42/54 MHz catalog profile.
gaps: Historical manufacturer-authored manual on a third-party mirror. A newer exact installed-module revision was not publicly recovered; confirm module, split and applicable procedure before adjustment.

The guide describes an analog video pilot. OEM QAM detectors also exist, but this review did not recover an exact detector setup/offset bulletin. Confirm installed detector part number, pilot type, frequency and level convention. A -6 dB datasheet loading relationship is not an AGC correction.
Manual-backoff and thermal setup are alternatives for the same fitted OEM AGC. Select the locally approved method; do not combine the two.

procedureModes.label: Manual backoff → OEM AGC
steps: Match the installed RF module, split, OEM AGC detector and design print; record approved low/high frequencies, output levels, tilt, pilot and loading.
Confirm valid input at both design frequencies and allow approximately one hour warm-up. Add 20 dB to raw -20 dB test-point readings only if the meter has not already compensated.

Before setting levels: S1 = 2 (manual setup). Turn MANUAL BACKOFF fully counterclockwise, then clockwise by the exact system amplifier p53 temperature/reference-frequency chart amount. Do not readjust backoff afterward.
At the main output, compare high-minus-low level with design tilt. Increase input EQ if tilt is low; decrease it if high. Remeasure.
At the highest design frequency, adjust forward input pad to the approved output: a larger pad lowers level; a smaller pad raises it. Recheck level and tilt.
Verify every output against its design reference. HGD/LGD auxiliary test points are after the signal director; account for director loss only when the print specifies a before-director level.
For the applicable conventional OEM detector, install AGC pad = corrected MAIN output pilot level (dBmV) minus 34 dB. Do not use an auxiliary-port level; confirm pilot compatibility first.
Record the corrected main-output pilot level in S1 = 2. Select S1 = 3 and adjust AGC GAIN to reproduce that level.
Toggle S1 between 2 and 3, allowing the module to settle before each reading. Repeat AGC GAIN adjustment until switching causes no level shift; the guide gives no fixed settling time.
Leave S1 = 3. Verify approved levels/tilt and each output again, record pilot/control/pad/EQ and before/after readings, then continue the job’s separate return workflow.

procedureModes.label: Thermal setup → OEM AGC
steps: Match the installed RF module, split, OEM AGC detector and design print; record approved low/high frequencies, output levels, tilt, pilot and loading.
Confirm valid input at both design frequencies and allow approximately one hour warm-up. Add 20 dB to raw -20 dB test-point readings only if the meter has not already compensated.
Before setting levels: S1 = 1 (OEM AGC thermal setup). Do not apply a manual-backoff chart in this branch.
At the main output, compare high-minus-low level with design tilt. Increase input EQ if tilt is low; decrease it if high. Remeasure.
At the highest design frequency, adjust forward input pad to the approved output: a larger pad lowers level; a smaller pad raises it. Recheck level and tilt.
Verify every output against its design reference. HGD/LGD auxiliary test points are after the signal director; account for director loss only when the print specifies a before-director level.
For the applicable conventional OEM detector, install AGC pad = corrected MAIN output pilot level (dBmV) minus 34 dB. Do not use an auxiliary-port level; confirm pilot compatibility first.
Record the corrected main-output pilot level in S1 = 1. Select S1 = 3 and adjust AGC GAIN to reproduce that level.
Toggle S1 between 1 and 3, allowing the module to settle before each reading. Repeat AGC GAIN adjustment until switching causes no level shift; the guide gives no fixed settling time.
Leave S1 = 3. Verify approved levels/tilt and each output again, record pilot/control/pad/EQ and before/after readings, then continue the job’s separate return workflow.

procedureModes.label: Thermal: amplifier only
steps: Match the installed RF module, split, thermal control configuration and design print; record approved low/high frequencies, output levels, tilt, pilot and loading.

Confirm no OEM AGC or DSIM is installed. Set S1 = 1 for amplifier-only thermal compensation.
Measure main-output high-minus-low tilt at approved design frequencies. If tilt is low, increase the input EQ; if high, decrease it. Remeasure.
At the highest design frequency, increase the forward input pad to lower output, or decrease it to raise output. Verify approved output level and tilt after each change.
Check all outputs against the correct port design; HGD/LGD auxiliary readings are after the signal director. Preserve factory interstage/output components unless design explicitly changes them.
Leave the selected thermal operating mode active. Record control mode, pad/EQ, corrected levels and before/after evidence; continue the separate return workflow.

At the highest design frequency, increase the forward input pad to lower output, or decrease it to raise output. Verify approved output level and tilt after each change.
Check all outputs against the correct port design; HGD/LGD auxiliary readings are after the signal director. Preserve factory interstage/output components unless design explicitly changes them.

steps: Match HGD/HGBT and physical diplex split. Connect QuantumLink Local to the intended interface. Check About for interface firmware/app version/MAC, then Amplifier Info for the installed device identity (pp38–40).

In Amplifier Config, match the displayed split to the installed diplex modules and confirm 1.8/1.2 GHz operating mode and active firmware bank. The guide starts ALSC OFF; enable only after both alignments below (p41).

Choose the intended measurement path under Test Points → Test Point Operation. Main FWD IN selects FWD IN or REV OUT; main/aux FWD OUT selects FWD OUT or REV IN. Add 20 dB to a raw -20 dB test-point reading only if the meter has not already compensated (pp6,50).

Confirm approved port output, marker frequencies, tilt and loading. In DS Auto Config, enter and verify the downstream profile marker frequencies and power levels, then Apply to store the profile. Confirm the actual approved pilots are present (p43).

Use downstream Manual only after Auto is complete and only if needed. Change one gain/tilt value at a time, apply with the checkbox, then Save Configuration to persist it. Revert restores the preset (p45).
Use Spectrum to check the resulting downstream response and approved output levels. Its roughly 30-second acquisition is a spectrum scan time, not an AGC wait instruction (p46).

After downstream balancing of the cascade, begin manufacturer upstream alignment at the last amplifier. Auto uses Upstream → Auto → Start Auto; save a successful alignment or revert and resolve it (p47).

If using manufacturer upstream Manual, this revision specifies ONX-630 DOCSIS Expert. Match instrument/firmware and the approved local return reference; adjust one value, apply, then Save Configuration (p48).

manualRegistry.title: Cisco GS7000 Intelligent Node — LCS level and tilt setup
manualRegistry.revision: Software guide main update September27,2018; Local Control chapter March21,2018
manualRegistry.sections: Local Control Software → RF Configuration, Node Configuration → Auto Setup, Forward Path; Quick Start → Node Level and Tilt.
manualRegistry.scope: Manufacturer procedure for the Intelligent-node LCS. Verify installed software/firmware compatibility; NightSweep records the process and does not control the node.
steps: Identify Intelligent launch/OIB/iRPD and compatible software; confirm iRPD online, downstream carriers present and operator targets before auto setup.
Use the LCS RF Configuration screen to enter low/high MHz and corresponding dBmV for each required port, enable ports and Save. At least Port1 must be configured, enabled and saved.
Return to Node Configuration and start Auto Setup. This adjusts forward OIB drive; it does not align the return path.
After completion, check Auto Setup/AGC status and alarms; allow several minutes for AGC and compare each port’s internal spectrum with its saved targets.
Capture final per-port readings/settings and repeat forward setup when input levels materially change, following the installed-release procedure.
gaps: Auto Setup itself takes less than a minute in this guide; Quick Start directs per-port spectrum review4–7minutes after setup. Completion of the command is not proof that AGC has settled.
Do not use displayed/default example frequencies and levels as plant targets.

manualRegistry.title: Cisco iNode Manager User Guide, Release24.1 — remote initial setup
manualRegistry.revision: Release24.1, June12,2024; newest manager user guide located in current Cisco index
manualRegistry.sections: Node Config → Settings / RF Port Settings; Maintenance → Initial Setup; Forward and Reverse Path → Spectrum.
manualRegistry.scope: Remote manager route for a compatible GS7000 Intelligent node, not standard optical GS7000 or Vecima-RPD retrofits. Verify installed manager/node versions before following.
steps: Select the correct iNode in Node Config and review its software, hardware and alarms.
Enter approved port frequencies and levels, enable at least Port1 and Save RF settings before initialization.
Open Maintenance → Initial Setup and start the approved setup operation.
Verify Initial Setup Status returns Normal, inspect AGC/alarms and compare port spectra against saved targets.
gaps: This is an alternative to local LCS operation, not an additional mandatory setup cycle.
The24.1 installation guide explicitly limits compatibility to Intelligent Node software4.0.0; verify the actual deployed release rather than upgrading as part of this workflow.

manualRegistry.title: Vecima EN9000 / EN9000U GAP — newest located manufacturer product brief
manualRegistry.revision: Printed publish date September2026; located via Parallel onNovember10,2026
manualRegistry.sections: p2: Power, Supported Vecima Modules, RFAM diplexers, RF Port Performance with ERM3 installed, Ordering Information.
manualRegistry.scope: Newer public brief than February2025. Covers EN9000/EN9000U family and adds ERM412/422. Housing roadmap does not establish installed RFAM/RPD operation. This is not an installation or AGC setup manual.
gaps: Exact EN9000/RFAM/RPD commissioning and level/tilt commands remain unverified behind the approved customer-documentation route.
TheRFAM split ranges remain85/102,204/258,396/492 and492/606MHz with documented endpoints; actual RPD limits may be lower.
The70dBmV composite maximum and15–21dB tilt over108–1218MHz are expressly ERM3-conditioned manufacturer references, not launch targets.
180W total PSU output,200W thermal limit and15A passing rating do not define typical AC input current.
No−20dB coupling value is restated in this brief; retain the separate May2024−20±1dB source and verify installed test port.

manualRegistry.title: Vecima ERM322/ERM324 RPD — manufacturer product brief
manualRegistry.sections: p1 capability; p2 control, module power and adapter-kit ordering.
manualRegistry.scope: RPD-module references only: ERM3 full spectrum support is1.2GHz DS/204MHz US even when node RFAM supports a wider band. Exact module and core support govern.
gaps: 50W typical/60W maximum and2A typical/2.4A maximum refer to the25V module, not whole-node AC draw.
GS7000 retrofit requires the matching adapter kit and1.2GHz-capable node for full spectrum operation; do not treat a1GHz host as1218MHz.
Obtain matching commissioning software manual; no setup commands are provided by this brief.

manualRegistry.title: Vecima ERM412/ERM422 RPD — manufacturer product brief
manualRegistry.revision: September2026 filename/search publication, but PDF body prints March2026; revision-date discrepancy retained
manualRegistry.sections: p1 capability; p2 control, supported chassis, per-configuration module current/power.
manualRegistry.scope: DOCSIS4.0 RPD module brief, not proof of installed EN9000 upgrade, compatible RFAM, or a commissioned1.8GHz spectrum.
gaps: Do not use ERM3 RF-performance conditions as ERM4 specifications.
Module DC watts/current depend on ERM412 versus422 and UHS/Shifted-FDX configuration; none equals total node AC draw.
Obtain firmware/core compatibility and commissioned configuration before changing plant targets or workflow.
